sections.title: Humans, Animals, & the Environment: An Interdisciplinary One Health Seminar Course
sections.description: This introductory course is intended to provide students with a foundation in topics relevant to human, animal, environmental health, and the interactions between the three. The course will provide students with an overview of the concept of One Health, with the goal of understanding how human, animal, and environmental well-being are interconnected. This course is open to students in any graduate program and will provide the opportunity to work collaboratively and form connections across disciplines. Each week will consist of both didactic lectures from professionals across various fields and small group discussions among peers. Topics discussed may include, but are not limited to: climate change and health, sustainable design, political ecology, interspecies relationships, sustainable business, antimicrobial resistance, urban planning, zoonotic disease, research methods in One Health, and biodiversity. These topics will be explored by lecturers with diverse fields of expertise, including human medicine, veterinary medicine, design, social policy and practice, business, anthropology, and environmental sciences.
